title: Sigmoid Fitting in Excel Using Solver Add-In
author: Kenji Ohgane
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.78ihrue
materials: Basically, no need to change the other options.

steps.title: Prepare Excel Template
steps.instruction: Download and open the ExcelSolver_Sigmoid.xlsx file, copying the sheet into your own file if necessary.

steps.title: Input Experimental Data
steps.instruction: Enter your data into the 'x' and 'y' columns, ensuring the 'x' column is in increasing or decreasing order to ensure the plot displays correctly.

steps.title: Estimate Initial Parameters
steps.instruction: Enter estimated initial values for the sigmoid parameters (minimum, max, n, and ec50) into cells B2, B3, B4, and B5 based on the plot.

steps.title: Configure Excel Solver
steps.instruction: Open the Solver tool from the 'Tools' menu and configure the following parameters:

substeps.instruction: Set 'Target cells' to $B$7 (Sum of Squared Residuals).
Set the 'equal to' section to 'Value of 0'.
Add constraints if necessary (e.g., ec_50 >= 0.000001) to prevent EC50 from becoming zero or negative.

steps.title: Run Fitting Algorithm
steps.instruction: Execute the Solver and process the results.

substeps.instruction: Ignore any 'unable to find solution' warnings.
Close the Solver window once the calculation is finished.
Verify that the sigmoid curve is reasonably fitted over the raw data points.
